nav.active_state_desc: Always visually indicate which tab or menu item is currently active.
nav.anchor_desc: Shortcuts to specific sections on long pages.
nav.breadcrumb_desc: Understand current location and quickly return to parent categories.
nav.burger_desc: Mobile aggregation for many menu items.
nav.context_switch_desc: Best for switching views within the same context.
nav.fixed_pos_desc: Fix navigation positions so they don't move between pages.

menuvocab.intro: The same menu goes by half a dozen names depending on who you learned it from. This page maps the nicknames people search for onto the canonical name and onto the component WIM actually ships.
menuvocab.why_canonical_title: Why the canonical name comes first
menuvocab.why_canonical: Nicknames are folklore: they travel by word of mouth, they disagree between teams, and several of them name the same shape. The canonical name is the one that lines up with the ARIA Authoring Practices and the platform guidelines, so it is the one worth writing in a ticket or a code review. Search this page by whichever name you know — both columns are plain text, so the browser's find works.
menuvocab.types_title: Menus that have a component behind them
menuvocab.overflow_nick: Kebab menu, Meatball menu, Three-dot menu, Vertical ellipsis, Horizontal ellipsis, More menu
menuvocab.overflow_look: Three dots — stacked vertically (⋮) on a row or card, laid out horizontally (⋯) inside a toolbar.
menuvocab.overflow_wim: `Dropdown` with the `more-vertical` icon, or `more-horizontal` when the trigger sits in a horizontal bar.
menuvocab.overflow_avoid: Don't park the primary action in here. Everything behind the dots costs a click plus a guess about what is inside, so it is a home for secondary commands only.
menuvocab.drawer_nick: Hamburger menu, Sandwich menu, Cheeseburger menu, Veggie burger menu, Nav toggle
menuvocab.drawer_look: Three horizontal lines of equal length (☰).
menuvocab.drawer_wim: `HamburgerMenu` as the trigger, opening a `Drawer` or a `Sidebar`.
menuvocab.drawer_avoid: Don't fold away navigation that already fits. At desktop widths a visible `Navbar` or `Sidebar` gets used far more than the same links behind a trigger.
menuvocab.switcher_nick: Bento menu, Waffle menu, Grid menu
menuvocab.switcher_look: A 3×3 arrangement of squares or dots.
menuvocab.switcher_wim: `BentoGrid` when the destinations deserve a panel with names and icons; `Dropdown` with the `grid` icon when the list is short.
menuvocab.switcher_avoid: Don't use it to move between pages of one app — that is what `Navbar` and `Sidebar` are for. The grid promises a jump to a different product.
menuvocab.filter_nick: Döner menu, Doner menu, Taco menu, Sort menu
menuvocab.filter_look: Horizontal lines of decreasing length, read as a funnel.
menuvocab.filter_wim: `Dropdown` with the `filter` icon for a handful of options; `QueryBuilder` once conditions start combining.
menuvocab.filter_avoid: Don't borrow the funnel for a general overflow menu. The shape promises that whatever is inside will narrow the data below it.
menuvocab.context_look: No trigger of its own. It opens at the pointer on right-click, or under the finger on long-press.
menuvocab.context_avoid: Never make it the only route to a command. It is invisible until someone guesses to right-click, and on touch it costs a deliberate long-press. Mirror every entry somewhere visible.
menuvocab.speeddial_look: A floating round button that fans out into several actions when pressed.
menuvocab.speeddial_wim: `SpeedDial`, or `FloatButton` when there is only one action to offer.
menuvocab.speeddial_avoid: Don't fan out more than a handful of actions. Past that the labels stop being readable at thumb reach and a `BottomSheet` serves better.
menuvocab.folklore_desc: These names circulate for a shape rather than for a job, so WIM ships no component and no icon for them. They are listed so a search lands somewhere — not because they are worth adopting.
menuvocab.folklore_hotdog: Hot dog menu — a single horizontal line. Where it means a drawer trigger, use `HamburgerMenu`.
menuvocab.folklore_pancake: Pancake menu — three stacked rounded bars. Same job as the drawer trigger.
menuvocab.folklore_cheeseburger: Cheeseburger menu — three lines with a dot beside each. Same job as the drawer trigger.
menuvocab.folklore_bacon: Bacon menu — wavy lines. Nothing maps to it.
menuvocab.folklore_chocolate: Chocolate bar menu, Candy bar menu — three vertical bars. Where it means an app switcher, use `BentoGrid`.
menuvocab.folklore_strawberry: Strawberry menu — dots scattered like seeds. Nothing maps to it.
menuvocab.machine_desc: The names that real design systems use — Apple's Human Interface Guidelines, Material, the ARIA Authoring Practices, Radix, MUI — are stored as `aliases` on each component in `src/data/components.json`, and `llms.txt` publishes them as `(aka …)` so an agent searching by a foreign name finds the component. That list is deliberately narrower than this page: it carries only names a real system uses, while the folklore above lives here and nowhere else. `npm run check:aliases` keeps an alias from colliding with a component name or with another alias.
menuvocab.pointer_from_overview: Came here looking for the kebab, hamburger or bento menu? That table maps the nicknames onto the component.

navutil.affix_desc: Pins sidebars or buttons at specific positions even during scrolling.
navutil.affix_usage_note: Use `Affix` to prevent important navigation from disappearing during scroll.
navutil.backtop_desc: Allows one-click scrolling to the top on long pages.
navutil.backtop_usage_note: Consider providing `BackTop` for pages requiring 3+ scrolls.
navutil.floatbtn_desc: Sticky buttons (e.g., bottom right) for prompts or inquiries.
navutil.floatbtn_usage_note: `FloatButton` is highly attention-grabbing; limit its use to avoid clutter.
navutil.guide_desc: Supplementary navigation elements that follow scrolls or jump instantly.
